newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala passes law to open power market.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala passes law to open power market.

text.p: Guatemala's congress on Wednesday passed a law to end state monopoloy on the electricity industry, allowing private companies to produce and sell power directly to consumers.

"What this law does is provide a clear legal framework so that Guatemalans and foreigners will have security to invest (in electric production and distribution)," legislator Guillermo de la Cruz, told Reuters in an interview.
The law was passed 49 to 23 with eight representatives absent in the 80-member congress following five weeks of debate.

The government of President Alvaro Arzu's National Advancement Party (PAN) has vigorously pushed the electricity law and a separate bill, still being debated in congress, to privatize the country's telecommunications industry.
